newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-ABDOUJAPAROV OUT OF TOUR AFTER FAILING DOPE TEST.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-ABDOUJAPAROV OUT OF TOUR AFTER FAILING DOPE TEST.

text.p: Uzbekistan's Djamolidine Abdoujaparov was expelled from the Tour de France on Friday after failing a dope test, organisers said.
Abdoujaparov, former winner of the Tour points standings, failed a test at the end of the second stage between St Valery-en-Caux and Vire last Monday.
Organisers did not immediately say what substance was found in the rider's urine but his Lotto team director Jean-Luc Vandenbroucke said two banned products had been detected.
Vandenbroucke added that a member of his staff had given Abdoujaparov the banned substance and had been sacked.
"It's my first doping case in nine years as a team director. This is very annoying especially as two products have been found," he said.
"We don't know where the first one comes from but the second was given by a member of my staff whom I sacked immediately.
"I cannot accept people acting behind my back."
Abdoujaparov finished second in Friday's sixth stage, at the end of which another rider, Belgian Tom Steels, was also expelled for "violent behaviour".
